# Essay Evaluation Rubric

Use this rubric to assess a user's draft against the five core dimensions of a
competitive graduate application essay. Score each dimension 0–3, then sum.

---

## Dimension 1 — Research Fit

| Score | Criterion |
|-------|-----------|
| 0 | No connection to the target program's research areas |
| 1 | Generic mention of the field without specific alignment |
| 2 | Specific alignment with named program research areas |
| 3 | Named faculty alignment and methodological fit with their current work |

---

## Dimension 2 — Intellectual Trajectory

| Score | Criterion |
|-------|-----------|
| 0 | No evidence of intellectual development over time |
| 1 | Descriptive list of activities without causal links |
| 2 | Causal narrative connecting past experiences to current goals |
| 3 | Distinctive intellectual identity with a clear and original future vision |

---

## Dimension 3 — Concreteness

| Score | Criterion |
|-------|-----------|
| 0 | All claims are vague or generic; no evidence |
| 1 | Some specific evidence present |
| 2 | Most key claims supported with concrete evidence |
| 3 | Every key claim anchored in a specific, verifiable experience or outcome |

---

## Dimension 4 — Structural Coherence

| Score | Criterion |
|-------|-----------|
| 0 | No discernible structure; topics appear randomly ordered |
| 1 | Loose grouping of topics; weak or absent transitions |
| 2 | Clear sections with logical transitions |
| 3 | Unified narrative arc — strong opening, sustained thread, resonant closing |

---

## Dimension 5 — Original Voice

| Score | Criterion |
|-------|-----------|
| 0 | Generic essay; could belong to any applicant |
| 1 | Some personal elements present |
| 2 | Distinctive perspective evident throughout |
| 3 | Unmistakable individual voice; only this author could have written this essay |

---

## Score Interpretation

| Total | Interpretation |
|-------|---------------|
| 0–5   | Significant revision needed across multiple dimensions |
| 6–10  | Developing — identify and strengthen the lowest-scoring dimensions |
| 11–13 | Competitive — refine details, sharpen concreteness and fit |
| 14–15 | Strong — final polish and proofreading only |

---

## How to Use This Rubric

1. Score each dimension independently before looking at the total.
2. Use the lowest-scoring dimensions to prioritise revision effort.
3. Reference `references/taxonomy.md` for concrete structural patterns to apply.
4. All revisions must use the user's own facts — never content from sample essays.
